description: Connect Four online free: drop red and yellow discs into seven columns and line up four in a row. Play against the computer or a friend.
lede: The board-game classic, in your browser. You drop red discs, the computer drops yellow, and the first to line up four in a row — across, down, or diagonally — takes the game. It starts with an empty board and a single obvious idea, and it ends with you counting threats in three directions at once. Your score against the computer is saved, so there is always a rematch to win.

p: Tap a column arrow — or any cell in a column — and your red disc drops to the lowest empty slot in that column. The computer answers with a yellow disc, and you take turns until somebody lines up four discs in a row: horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. The first to do it wins. If all 42 slots fill up with no line of four, the game is a draw.

You can also play against a friend on the same screen: open the options at the bottom and switch to 2 Players. Red always goes first. The computer has three difficulties — Easy plays loosely and misses blocks, Medium blocks most threats, and Hard reads several moves ahead, so expect it to set traps.

There are 69 different lines of four on a Connect Four board: 24 horizontal, 21 vertical, and 24 diagonal. Most wins are built, not found — you place three discs with an open end and force your opponent to choose which threat to block. A vertical four is the simplest: drop four discs in the same column before your opponent notices. A horizontal four needs an open row and a free slot underneath every disc. Diagonal fours are the ones that sneak up on people, because the winning disc often lands two columns away from where the line started.

sections.h: A solved game with a first-player edge
p: Connect Four was first sold by Milton Bradley in 1974, but the game itself is older: it descends from a tabletop game called The Captain's Mistress, played with a frame of rings and coloured balls. The familiar plastic grid with red and yellow checkers has barely changed since.

In 1988, the Dutch computer scientist Victor Allis solved Connect Four: with perfect play the first player always wins. The winning first move is the centre column. That does not make the game dull — it makes the opening matter. Play the centre, build threats in two directions at once, and never give your opponent a free three in a row with both ends open.

ol: Open in the centre column. It is part of more winning lines than any other column, and the first player wins with perfect play from there.
Build two threats at once. If you have two different ways to make four, your opponent can only block one of them.
Watch the diagonals. Most players spot horizontal and vertical threats; the diagonal that wins is usually the one nobody was watching.
Never drop a disc directly under your opponent's three in a row unless it wins you the game — you are handing them the fourth.
Count the open ends. A three in a row with both ends open is almost unstoppable; a three with one end blocked is just a threat you can ignore for a move.
On Hard, do not trade moves in the middle. The computer reads traps several moves ahead, so play for two threats instead of one.

faq: How do I drop a disc?
Tap a column arrow at the top of the board, or tap any cell in the column you want. The disc falls to the lowest empty slot in that column. Keys 1 to 7 drop a disc in columns 1 to 7.
Red always goes first. In vs Computer mode that is you; in 2 Players mode the first player is Red. The starting player alternates each new game.
Can I play against a friend?
Yes. Open the options at the bottom of the game and switch to 2 Players. You take turns on the same screen — Red, then Yellow.
There are three difficulties. Easy misses blocks and plays loosely, Medium blocks most threats, and Hard reads several moves ahead and sets traps. Start on Medium.
What happens if the board fills up?
If all 42 slots are full and nobody has four in a row, the game is a draw and the score keeps a draw count.
Yes. Your wins, draws and losses against the computer are saved in this browser on this device, separately for each difficulty, and shown at the top of the screen.
